title.zh-CN: 被发现意识不清伴双上肢抽搐 · 50岁女性
title.en: Found unconscious with convulsions of both arms · 50-year-old woman

summary.zh-CN: 50岁女性，一年前查出糖尿病。她被发现躺在床上意识不清、双上肢抽搐，现在在急诊。
summary.en: A 50-year-old woman whose diabetes was found a year ago was discovered unconscious in bed with convulsions of both arms; she is now in the emergency department.

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 从意识不清、血糖33.7 mmol/L、无酮症、无酸中毒和高渗透压识别高渗高血糖状态（JBDS-IP 2022所列特征），并指出单纯高血糖危象解释不了的一点：血钠172 mmol/L时尿比重却是1.005。
learningOutcomes.en: Recognise a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state from unconsciousness, a glucose of 33.7 mmol/L, no ketosis or acidosis and a high osmolality (the JBDS-IP 2022 features), and name what a hyperglycaemic crisis alone does not explain: urine of specific gravity 1.005 beside a sodium of 172 mmol/L.

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 制定最初24小时的安全方案：先用0.9%氯化钠；血钾3.2 mmol/L时先补钾、暂缓胰岛素（补液后血糖不再下降时才以0.05单位/kg/h开始，JBDS-IP 2022）；每小时监测；血钠24小时下降不超过10 mmol/L（JBDS-IP 2022；2024年共识）。
learningOutcomes.en: Plan the first 24 hours safely: 0.9% sodium chloride first; with a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L, potassium before insulin, and insulin only once the glucose stops falling on fluids, at 0.05 U/kg/h (JBDS-IP 2022); hourly monitoring; a sodium that falls by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (JBDS-IP 2022; 2024 consensus).

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 血糖控制后多尿和高钠仍持续时，识别尿液浓缩障碍（AVP缺乏或AVP抵抗），用配对的血、尿渗透压和去氨加压素来证实，而不对已经高钠的患者做禁水试验（美国内分泌学会2016）。
learningOutcomes.en: When polyuria and hypernatraemia persist after the glucose is controlled, recognise a urine-concentrating defect (AVP deficiency or resistance) and confirm it with paired plasma and urine osmolality and desmopressin — not with water deprivation in a patient who is already hypernatraemic (Endocrine Society 2016).

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 解读AVP缺乏合并空蝶鞍：影像只说明结构，需检查垂体前叶功能，首先查晨8–9时皮质醇（美国内分泌学会2016）。
learningOutcomes.en: Interpret AVP deficiency with an empty sella: imaging shows structure, not function, so test the anterior pituitary, beginning with an 8–9 am cortisol (Endocrine Society 2016).

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 处理去氨加压素相关的低钠血症：暂停或减量，每6小时查血钠，24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L（欧洲低钠血症指南2014）；并以最低有效剂量、至少每周一次的多尿期来预防（美国内分泌学会2016）。
learningOutcomes.en: Manage desmopressin-associated hyponatraemia — hold or reduce the dose, check sodium every 6 hours, a rise of no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (European hyponatraemia guideline 2014) — and prevent it with the lowest effective dose and a phase of polyuria at least weekly (Endocrine Society 2016).

learningOutcomes.zh-CN: 用她听得懂的话解释糖尿病与AVP缺乏（尿崩症）的区别，以及为什么去氨加压素既不能漏用也不能多用（2022年更名声明；英国内分泌学会2018）。
learningOutcomes.en: Explain to her in plain words how her diabetes mellitus differs from AVP deficiency (diabetes insipidus), and why desmopressin must be neither missed nor overdosed (2022 renaming statement; Society for Endocrinology 2018).

The person who came with her, where each phase takes place (emergency department, high-dependency bed, ward), who tells the long drinking history, the staff, and the decisions, interventions, scoring and teaching points are educational design.

triageNote.zh-CN: 50岁女性，3小时前被发现躺在床上意识不清、双上肢抽搐。一年前查出糖尿病，二甲双胍服用不规律。到院时意识不清，脉搏104次/分，血压121/74 mmHg。陪她来的人在床旁。
triageNote.en: 50-year-old woman found unconscious in bed three hours ago with convulsions of both arms. Diabetes diagnosed a year ago; takes metformin irregularly. On arrival: unconscious, pulse 104/min, blood pressure 121/74 mmHg. The person who came with her is at the bedside.

personality.zh-CN: 50岁。急诊时意识不清，不能说话；醒来以后说话平和、简短，问什么答什么。
personality.en: 50 years old. Unconscious and unable to speak in the emergency department; once awake she is calm and brief, answering what she is asked.

speechStyle.zh-CN: 日常口语，不用医学术语；医生告诉过她的病名会照着说。
speechStyle.en: Everyday speech without medical terms; she repeats the names the doctors have told her.

openingLine.zh-CN: （她意识不清，不能说话；陪她来的人在床旁。）
openingLine.en: (She is unconscious and cannot speak; the person who came with her is at the bedside.)

actingNotes.zh-CN: 急诊阶段：她意识不清，不能说话，由陪同者回答。病房阶段起：她已清醒，用自己的话回答，只说问到的内容，不增减数字和时间；问到病历里没有的事，就说说不上来，不要编。用去氨加压素期间（第三阶段）：她觉得头晕。
actingNotes.en: Emergency department: she is unconscious and cannot speak; her companion answers. From the ward phase on: she is awake and answers in her own words, only what is asked, never adding or changing numbers or times; for anything not in her record she says she is not sure and invents nothing. On desmopressin (the third phase): she feels dizzy.

persona.zh-CN: 陪她来医院的人，和她是什么关系没有记录。着急，说话直白，用日常的话；只知道自己说得出的那些情况：她是怎么被发现的、她的糖尿病和二甲双胍、这一年多口干喝水多；不知道的就说不知道，不替她编。最想知道她能不能醒过来。
persona.en: The person who came to hospital with her; their relationship to her is not recorded. Worried and plain-spoken, in everyday words; knows only what they can tell — how she was found, her diabetes and metformin, her dry mouth and drinking over the past year or more — says so when they do not know and never makes anything up. Most of all wants to know whether she will wake up.

description.en: She has just arrived in the emergency resuscitation bay, unconscious; the person who came with her is at the bedside.

dose.en: In the IV fluids by pump, at the concentration and rate the senior sets — a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L is below the 3.5 mmol/L at which JBDS-IP 2022 asks for senior review and more than its standard replacement, given through a central line in a high-dependency area; never as a bolus; potassium rechecked soon, on the cardiac monitor.

dose.en: Osmolality every hour at first (JBDS-IP 2022) — calculated from sodium, glucose and urea, or measured — with capillary glucose hourly, potassium rechecked closely, and a urinary catheter with hourly urine output and a fluid balance chart.

dose.en: A prophylactic dose by subcutaneous injection once daily, as the local protocol sets for her weight and kidney function, for the whole admission unless contraindicated (JBDS-IP 2022).

name.zh-CN: 固定速率静脉胰岛素输注

dose.zh-CN: HHS按0.05 单位/kg/h 静脉泵入（JBDS-IP 2022）；0.1 单位/kg/h 是酮症酸中毒的速率（2024年共识）
dose.en: 0.05 U/kg/h IV by syringe pump in HHS (JBDS-IP 2022); 0.1 U/kg/h is the ketoacidosis rate (2024 consensus)

harm.zh-CN: 在最初几小时、血钾3.2 mmol/L时用胰岛素：胰岛素会把钾带进细胞；JBDS-IP 2022规定血钾低于3.5 mmol/L时需上级医生评估并额外补钾；对没有明显酮血症的HHS，要等单纯补液后血糖不再下降才开始胰岛素（0.05单位/kg/h），因为过早使用会使渗透压骤降，有循环衰竭的风险。
harm.en: Insulin in the first hours, with a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L: insulin moves potassium into cells, and below 3.5 mmol/L JBDS-IP 2022 asks for senior review and extra potassium; in HHS without significant ketonaemia it starts insulin (0.05 U/kg/h) only once the glucose stops falling on IV fluids alone, because early insulin drops the osmolality precipitously and risks circulatory collapse.

response.zh-CN: 胰岛素已开始输注。本病例没有记录她是否、何时以及以什么速度用过胰岛素。
response.en: The infusion is running. This case does not record whether, when or at what rate she received insulin.

name.zh-CN: 快速输注低渗液体，把血钠尽快降到正常
name.en: Hypotonic fluid run fast to bring the sodium to normal

dose.zh-CN: 5%葡萄糖或0.45%氯化钠，1 L/h静脉输注，直到血钠正常
dose.en: 5% glucose or 0.45% sodium chloride IV at 1 L/h until the sodium is normal

harm.zh-CN: 快速输注低渗液体，无论血钠起点如何，都会使血钠变化快于大脑能适应的速度。血钠高时，JBDS-IP 2022和2024年共识规定血钠24小时下降不超过10 mmol/L、渗透压每小时下降3–8 mOsm/kg，降得更快有脑水肿和渗透性脱髓鞘的风险；JBDS-IP只在充分输注0.9%氯化钠后渗透压仍不下降时才改用0.45%氯化钠，而5%葡萄糖会给糖尿病患者增加糖负荷。
harm.en: A hypotonic fluid run fast moves the sodium faster than the brain can adapt, whatever its starting level. While the sodium is high, JBDS-IP 2022 and the 2024 consensus limit its fall to 10 mmol/L in 24 hours and the fall in osmolality to 3–8 mOsm/kg an hour, because faster falls risk cerebral oedema and osmotic demyelination; JBDS-IP turns to 0.45% sodium chloride only when osmolality stops falling despite adequate 0.9% sodium chloride, and 5% glucose adds a glucose load in a woman with diabetes.

dose.zh-CN: 能安全饮水时按量口服补水（不能饮水时才静脉输注5%葡萄糖，并监测血糖），使血钠每小时下降不超过0.5 mmol/L、24小时不超过10 mmol/L；补液期间每4小时查血钠（英国内分泌学会2018）。
dose.en: Water by mouth in measured amounts when she can drink safely (5% glucose IV only if she cannot, with glucose checks), so that her sodium falls by no more than 0.5 mmol/L an hour and 10 mmol/L in 24 hours; sodium every 4 hours while fluids are being replaced (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

response.zh-CN: 补水已开始。本病例没有记录她喝了或输了多少水。
response.en: Water replacement is under way. This case does not record how much water she drank or was given.

harm.zh-CN: 现在不行。补水是给高钠且能喝水的人用的。刚到院时她意识不清，不能经口给水；HHS首先输注0.9%氯化钠：JBDS-IP 2022只有在充分输注0.9%氯化钠后渗透压仍不下降时才改用0.45%氯化钠，血糖降到14 mmol/L以下时才开始输5%或10%葡萄糖。血钠偏低时，再补水只会让血钠更低（欧洲低钠血症指南2014要求停用非必需的液体）。
harm.en: Not now. Water replacement is for a high sodium in someone who can drink. On arrival she is unconscious — nothing by mouth — and in HHS the first fluid is 0.9% sodium chloride: JBDS-IP 2022 turns to 0.45% sodium chloride only if the osmolality stops falling despite adequate 0.9%, and starts 5% or 10% glucose only once the glucose is below 14 mmol/L. When the sodium is low, more water lowers it further (the European hyponatraemia guideline 2014 stops non-essential fluids).

name.zh-CN: 禁水试验（从现在起禁饮）
name.en: Water deprivation test (no fluids from now)

en: nil by mouth for the test

dose.zh-CN: 停止一切饮水和输液，每小时称体重、测尿量和尿比重，直到尿液浓缩或体重下降3%。
dose.en: Withhold all fluids, weighing her and measuring urine volume and specific gravity hourly, until the urine concentrates or she loses 3% of her weight.

harm.zh-CN: 禁水试验在她的诊治中没有用武之地。美国内分泌学会2016年的方案在血浆渗透压超过295 mOsm/L而尿仍稀释时就停止禁水（这本身即可确诊尿崩症），随后给去氨加压素；血钠高于约148 mmol/L时，仅血钠的两倍就已超过这一界值；而一旦开始用去氨加压素，这个试验也就没有什么可判断的了。肾脏还在不断排出稀释尿时停止一切饮水，会使血钠快速攀升，走向抽搐和循环衰竭。
harm.en: A water deprivation test has no place in her care. The Endocrine Society 2016 protocol stops thirsting as soon as plasma osmolality passes 295 mOsm/L with dilute urine — that alone confirms diabetes insipidus — and then gives desmopressin; with a sodium above about 148 mmol/L, twice the sodium is past that point on its own, and once desmopressin has been started there is nothing left for the test to decide. Withholding all water while the kidneys keep losing dilute urine makes the sodium climb fast, towards seizures and collapse.

dose.zh-CN: 限制每日经口饮水量，例如1–1.5 L；或暂时禁食禁饮。
dose.en: Oral intake limited to a set daily volume (for example 1–1.5 L), or nil by mouth for now.

response.zh-CN: 已限制她经口的饮水量。
response.en: Her oral fluid intake is restricted.

harm.zh-CN: 血钠高时不能限水：她血钠162 mmol/L、每天尿量8.4 L，丢的水比喝进去的多，限制饮水只会让血钠更高，走向抽搐和循环衰竭。英国内分泌学会（2018）把这种高钠血症当作急症处理，并补足缺失的水分——能喝水时经口补充——而不是限制。
harm.en: Not while her sodium is high: with a sodium of 162 mmol/L and 8.4 L of urine a day she is losing more water than she takes in, and restricting what she drinks drives the sodium higher, towards seizures and collapse. The Society for Endocrinology (2018) treats such hypernatraemia as a medical emergency and replaces the water deficit — by mouth when the patient can drink — rather than withholding it.

dose.zh-CN: 从小剂量开始——静脉或肌内注射1–2微克，或口服100微克（英国内分泌学会2018剂量范围）——找出能控制多尿的最低剂量；调整剂量期间至少每天查一次血钠。
dose.en: Start low — desmopressin 1–2 micrograms IV or IM, or 100 micrograms by mouth (Society for Endocrinology 2018 dose ranges) — and find the lowest dose that controls the polyuria, checking her sodium at least daily while the dose is set.

harm.zh-CN: 现在不该用：去氨加压素让肾脏保留水分，只在尿崩症已经明确、血钠有人盯着时使用——不在刚到院、血糖33.7 mmol/L且正在大量补液时用（即使已确诊中枢性尿崩症，英国内分泌学会2018也是先用0.9%氯化钠恢复容量，并提醒大量补液加去氨加压素可能使高钠纠正过快），也不在血钠偏低时再追加一剂（欧洲低钠血症指南2014要求停用诱发低钠的药物）。
harm.en: Not at this point: desmopressin makes the kidneys hold water, so it is given only once diabetes insipidus is established and the sodium is being watched — not on arrival, with a glucose of 33.7 mmol/L and large fluid volumes going in (even in known cranial diabetes insipidus the Society for Endocrinology 2018 restores volume with 0.9% sodium chloride first and warns that desmopressin with large fluid loads can correct a high sodium too fast), and not as a further dose while the sodium is low (the European hyponatraemia guideline 2014 stops medicines that provoke hyponatraemia).

response.zh-CN: 已给去氨加压素。本病例不模拟它的效果。
response.en: Desmopressin is given. This case does not simulate its effect.

dose.zh-CN: 今天与内分泌团队讨论她的情况（英国内分泌学会2018）。
dose.en: Discuss her with the endocrine team today (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

response.zh-CN: 内分泌团队会来看她。本病例没有记录有哪些团队参与了她的诊治。
response.en: The endocrine team will see her. This case does not record which teams were involved in her care.

name.zh-CN: 向她讲解去氨加压素和她的病
name.en: Teach her about desmopressin and her condition

dose.zh-CN: 确诊以后，用通俗的话讲清：她的病是什么、和她的糖尿病有什么不同；去氨加压素为什么既不能漏用也不能多用；至少每周让药效过去一次、出现一段多尿（美国内分泌学会2016）；口渴时才喝水；定期查血钠；佩戴急救手环或项链（美国内分泌学会2016）；最后请她复述要点。
dose.en: In plain words, once the diagnosis is made: what her condition is and how it differs from her diabetes mellitus; why desmopressin must never be missed and never taken in extra doses; a phase of polyuria at least weekly, when the dose is allowed to wear off (Endocrine Society 2016); drinking to thirst; sodium checks; an emergency bracelet or necklace (Endocrine Society 2016); and teach-back.

response.zh-CN: 已讲解。本病例没有记录对她或陪她来的人讲过什么。
response.en: The explanation is given. This case does not record what she or the person who came with her was told.

name.zh-CN: 暂停或减少去氨加压素

dose.zh-CN: 暂停下一剂（或减量），饮水只以口渴为度，每6小时查血钠，第一个24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L，之后每24小时不超过8 mmol/L（欧洲低钠血症指南2014），并观察尿量——药效一过、快速排水可能使血钠升得过快——再以更低剂量重新开始。
dose.en: Hold the next dose (or reduce it), let her drink only to thirst, check sodium every 6 hours aiming for a rise of no more than 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L in each 24 hours after (European hyponatraemia guideline 2014), and watch her urine output — a brisk water diuresis as the drug wears off can overshoot — then restart at a lower dose.

response.zh-CN: 已调整。本病例没有记录她之后的剂量。
response.en: Done. This case does not record her later doses.

name.en: 3% sodium chloride 150 mL IV over 20 minutes

dose.zh-CN: 3%氯化钠150 mL静脉输注，20分钟输完
dose.en: 3% sodium chloride 150 mL IV over 20 minutes

harm.zh-CN: 3%氯化钠会让血钠快速升高。欧洲低钠血症指南（2014）把它用于伴严重症状（呕吐、深度嗜睡、抽搐、昏迷、心肺窘迫）或中重度症状（恶心、意识模糊、头痛）的低钠血症，无论急性还是慢性；没有这些症状时，只用于有记录的急性下降超过10 mmol/L。它不用于高钠；没有上述症状、下降时间又没有记录的低钠，指南按慢性处理：停用诱发药物，第一个24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L。
harm.en: 3% saline raises the sodium quickly. The European hyponatraemia guideline (2014) gives it for hyponatraemia with severe symptoms (vomiting, deep somnolence, seizures, coma, cardiorespiratory distress) or moderately severe ones (nausea, confusion, headache), whether acute or chronic, and without such symptoms only for a documented acute fall of more than 10 mmol/L. It is not for a high sodium; and a low sodium without those symptoms whose fall is of undocumented timing is treated as chronic: stop the drug that provokes it and keep the rise within 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours.

title.zh-CN: 到院：发生了什么，她是谁
title.en: Arrival: what happened, and who is she?

hint.zh-CN: 她是怎么、什么时候被发现的？她的糖尿病、用药和最近一年的情况怎样？她的意识、脉搏和血压告诉你什么？
hint.en: How and when was she found? What is known about her diabetes, her tablets and the past year? What do her consciousness, pulse and blood pressure tell you?

guidance.zh-CN: 她意识不清，躺在抢救室；陪她来的人可以替她回答。
guidance.en: She is unconscious in the resuscitation bay; the person who came with her can answer for her.

hint.zh-CN: 一个意识不清的糖尿病患者，哪些床旁和实验室检查要马上做？每个结果说明什么？哪一个结果和其他结果对不上？
hint.en: Which bedside and laboratory tests does an unconscious person with diabetes need at once? What does each result tell you — and which one does not fit with the others?

guidance.zh-CN: 抢救室里有血糖仪、心电图机，化验室和CT都可以用。
guidance.en: The bay has a glucometer and an ECG machine; the laboratory and CT are available.

hint.zh-CN: 先输什么？什么时候可以用胰岛素，她的血钾对此意味着什么？这些数值每小时最多能变多快？她应该在哪里接受照护？
hint.en: What goes in first, when may insulin start and what does her potassium mean for it, how fast may the numbers move, and where should she be looked after?

guidance.zh-CN: 仍在抢救室，护士和输液泵都在床旁。
guidance.en: Still in the resuscitation bay, with the nurse and the infusion pumps at the bed.

hint.zh-CN: 看看头几天和病房的记录：哪些数字放在一起说不通？她自己能告诉你什么？
hint.en: Read the records of the first days and of the ward review: which numbers do not fit together? What can she tell you herself?

guidance.zh-CN: 她在病房，已经清醒，可以自己回答问题。
guidance.en: She is on the ward, awake and able to answer for herself.

hint.zh-CN: 试验中她的尿有什么变化？影像显示了什么，又说明不了什么？长期治疗之前还要先查什么？
hint.en: What did her urine do on the test? What does the scan show, and what can it not tell you? What must be checked before long-term treatment?

guidance.zh-CN: 试验记录和MRI报告在病历中。
guidance.en: The test record and the MRI report are in the notes.

title.zh-CN: 治疗中，以及报告的结局
title.en: On treatment, and the reported outcome

hint.zh-CN: 她现在怎么样，血钠多少，你要改什么？然后把你的方案和报告的做法比一比。
hint.en: How is she, what is her sodium, and what do you change? Then set your plan beside what the report did.

guidance.zh-CN: 她在病房，已经开始用去氨加压素。
guidance.en: She is on the ward and has started desmopressin.

prompt.zh-CN: 到院时：血糖33.7 mmol/L；钠172、钾3.2 mmol/L；肌酐122.9 μmol/L；pH 7.4，碳酸氢根36.5 mmol/L；尿酮阴性，尿比重1.005；头颅CT未见异常。哪一种解读能解释全部结果？
prompt.en: On arrival: glucose 33.7 mmol/L; sodium 172 and potassium 3.2 mmol/L; creatinine 122.9 μmol/L; pH 7.4, bicarbonate 36.5 mmol/L; urine ketones negative, specific gravity 1.005; head CT unremarkable. Which reading accounts for all of it?

need.zh-CN: 先看她的血糖，钠、钾和肌酐，pH和碳酸氢根，尿常规和头颅CT。
need.en: Read her glucose, sodium, potassium and creatinine, pH and bicarbonate, urinalysis and head CT first.

text.zh-CN: 高渗高血糖状态——同时还有超出血糖所能解释的失水，因为本该浓缩的尿却是稀释的
text.en: A hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state — and water is being lost beyond what the glucose explains, since her urine is dilute when it should be concentrated

feedback.zh-CN: 正确。血糖33.7 mmol/L，没有明显酮症（尿酮阴性）和酸中毒（pH 7.4，碳酸氢根36.5 mmol/L），渗透压超过320 mOsm/kg——不算尿素，2×172+33.7就已是377.7——符合JBDS-IP 2022所列高渗高血糖状态的特征。但如此高渗的患者本该排出浓缩尿；尿比重1.005说明排出的几乎是不含溶质的水，所以要记录尿量，并问清她口渴有多久了。
feedback.en: Right. A glucose of 33.7 mmol/L without significant ketosis (urine ketones negative) or acidosis (pH 7.4, bicarbonate 36.5 mmol/L), with an osmolality above 320 mOsm/kg — 2 × 172 + 33.7 = 377.7 even before urea — has the features JBDS-IP 2022 gives for a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state. But a patient this hyperosmolar should be passing concentrated urine: a specific gravity of 1.005 means water is leaving with little solute, so measure her urine output and ask how long she has been thirsty.

text.zh-CN: 糖尿病酮症酸中毒：已知糖尿病、意识不清、血糖这么高，在酮体结果排除之前，都应按酮症酸中毒治疗
text.en: Diabetic ketoacidosis: with known diabetes, unconsciousness and a glucose this high, she should be treated for ketoacidosis until her ketones prove otherwise

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。酮症酸中毒需要酮体升高和酸中毒，她两样都没有：尿酮阴性，pH 7.4，碳酸氢根36.5 mmol/L（2024年共识规定，诊断酮症酸中毒须同时具备高血糖或糖尿病、酮体升高和代谢性酸中毒三项）。按酮症酸中毒处理会促使过早给足量胰岛素，而血钾3.2 mmol/L的高渗状态恰恰不能这样做。
feedback.en: No. Ketoacidosis needs raised ketones and acidosis, and she has neither: urine ketones are negative, the pH is 7.4 and the bicarbonate 36.5 mmol/L (the 2024 consensus requires all three components — hyperglycaemia or diabetes, raised ketones and metabolic acidosis — for ketoacidosis). Treating this as ketoacidosis pushes towards early full-dose insulin, which a hyperosmolar state with a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L must not get.

text.zh-CN: 普通的高渗状态：血糖引起的渗透性利尿既能解释高钠，也能解释稀释尿，不再需要别的解释
text.en: An ordinary hyperosmolar state: the glucose-driven osmotic diuresis accounts for both the high sodium and the dilute urine, so nothing else needs explaining

feedback.zh-CN: 不完全对。葡萄糖引起的渗透性利尿会把溶质带进尿里，尿比重不会低；1.005的尿几乎是不含溶质的水，糖尿造成不了——何况这份尿检记录尿糖阴性，这一矛盾还有待核实。超出血糖所能解释的失水需要另找原因。
feedback.en: Not quite. An osmotic diuresis from glucose carries solute into the urine and keeps its specific gravity up; urine at 1.005 is almost solute-free water, which glycosuria does not produce — and this urine was even recorded as glucose-negative, a discordance still to be checked. A water loss beyond the glucose needs its own explanation.

text.zh-CN: 原发的癫痫发作或卒中：先有抽搐，化验的异常是长时间抽搐加上几个小时没喝水留下的
text.en: A primary seizure or a stroke: the convulsions came first, and the chemistry is what a long fit and hours without drinking have left behind

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。抽搐不会让血钠升到172 mmol/L、血糖升到33.7 mmol/L；能引起意识不清和抽搐的恰恰是高渗状态，而且她的头颅CT未见异常。CT未见异常并不能排除所有结构性或感染性病因，需要不断再评估——但现在要先处理代谢紊乱。
feedback.en: No. A fit does not raise the sodium to 172 mmol/L or the glucose to 33.7 mmol/L; it is the hyperosmolar state that can cause unconsciousness and convulsions, and her head CT was unremarkable. An unremarkable CT does not rule out every structural or infective cause, so keep reassessing — but treat the metabolic state now.

prompt.zh-CN: 你判断这是高渗高血糖状态，血钾3.2 mmol/L，尿是稀释的。最初24小时你怎么处理？
prompt.en: You read this as a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state with a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L and dilute urine. What is your plan for the first 24 hours?

need.zh-CN: 先回答怎样解读首批结果（决策1）。
need.en: Decide how to read the first results (decision 1) first.

text.zh-CN: 先用0.9%氯化钠恢复循环、补钾，补液后血糖不再下降才用胰岛素；每小时查血糖、血钠和渗透压，血钠24小时下降不超过10 mmol/L
text.en: 0.9% saline to restore the circulation, potassium replaced, insulin only once the glucose stops falling on fluids; glucose, sodium and osmolality hourly, sodium down no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours

feedback.zh-CN: 正确。先用0.9%氯化钠——2024年共识推荐没有心、肾功能受损的成人在最初2–4小时按500–1000 mL/h输注；她肌酐122.9 μmol/L且没有基线值，要勤加评估；血钾低于3.5 mmol/L需上级医生评估，补钾量要超过常规方案（JBDS-IP 2022）；JBDS-IP对没有明显酮血症的HHS，要等补液后血糖不再下降才以0.05单位/kg/h开始胰岛素；开始时每小时查渗透压，每小时下降3–8 mOsm/kg，血糖每小时下降不超过5 mmol/L（2024年共识为5–6.7），血钠24小时下降不超过10 mmol/L（JBDS-IP 2022；2024年共识）。她的尿是稀释的，尿量是要盯住的数字。
feedback.en: Right. 0.9% sodium chloride first — the 2024 consensus recommends 500–1000 mL/h for the first 2–4 hours in adults without heart or kidney compromise, so reassess often with a creatinine of 122.9 μmol/L and no baseline; a potassium below 3.5 mmol/L needs senior review and more than the standard replacement (JBDS-IP 2022); JBDS-IP starts insulin in HHS without significant ketonaemia only once the glucose stops falling on fluids, at 0.05 U/kg/h; osmolality hourly at first, falling 3–8 mOsm/kg an hour, glucose by no more than 5 mmol/L an hour (5–6.7 in the 2024 consensus) and sodium by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (JBDS-IP 2022; 2024 consensus). With her dilute urine, the urine output is the number to watch.

text.zh-CN: 今天之内用5%葡萄糖或0.45%氯化钠快速输注，把血钠降到正常，因为让她意识不清的正是172 mmol/L的高钠；傍晚复查，正常以后再减慢速度
text.en: Bring her sodium back to normal today with 5% glucose or 0.45% saline run fast, since a sodium of 172 mmol/L is what keeps her unconscious; recheck it this evening and slow the drip once it is back to normal

feedback.zh-CN: 不对——目标是速度，而不是正常值。一天内把172 mmol/L降到正常，就是下降约30 mmol/L，是JBDS-IP 2022和2024年共识允许的24小时10 mmol/L的三倍；已经适应高渗的脑细胞会因此水肿或发生脱髓鞘。JBDS-IP只有在充分输注0.9%氯化钠后渗透压仍不下降时才改用0.45%氯化钠，而5%葡萄糖会让33.7 mmol/L的血糖更高。
feedback.en: No — the target is the rate, not the normal number. Taking 172 mmol/L to normal in a day is a fall of about 30 mmol/L, three times the 10 mmol/L in 24 hours that JBDS-IP 2022 and the 2024 consensus allow, and brain cells adapted to the high osmolality then swell or demyelinate. JBDS-IP turns to 0.45% sodium chloride only when osmolality stops falling despite adequate 0.9%, and 5% glucose would add to a glucose of 33.7 mmol/L.

text.zh-CN: 现在就在补液的同时开始0.1单位/kg/h的固定速率胰岛素输注，让血糖和渗透压尽快降下来，等胰岛素输上以后再补钾
text.en: Start a fixed-rate insulin infusion at 0.1 U/kg/h now, alongside the fluids, so that the glucose and the osmolality come down quickly, and add the potassium once the insulin is running

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。血钾3.2 mmol/L时，胰岛素会把钾带进细胞，可能诱发心律失常；JBDS-IP 2022规定血钾低于3.5 mmol/L时需上级医生评估并额外补钾，HHS要等单纯补液后血糖不再下降时才以0.05单位/kg/h开始胰岛素，因为过早使用会使渗透压骤降，可能导致循环衰竭。对于酮症酸中毒，2024年共识也要求血钾升到3.5 mmol/L以上再用胰岛素。
feedback.en: No. With a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L, insulin drives potassium into cells and can provoke arrhythmia; JBDS-IP 2022 asks for senior review and extra potassium below 3.5 mmol/L, and in HHS starts insulin only once the glucose stops falling on fluids alone, at 0.05 U/kg/h, because early insulin drops the osmolality precipitously and can cause circulatory collapse. In ketoacidosis, too, the 2024 consensus delays insulin until potassium is above 3.5 mmol/L.

text.zh-CN: 现在静脉注射去氨加压素1–2微克止住稀释尿，然后用5%葡萄糖补回丢失的液体，每隔几小时查一次血钠
text.en: Give desmopressin 1–2 micrograms IV now to stop the dilute urine, then replace what she has lost with 5% glucose, checking her sodium every few hours

feedback.zh-CN: 现在不行。血糖33.7 mmol/L时还不能把这些尿当作单纯失水——美国内分泌学会2016年诊断中枢性尿崩症的标准包括尿试纸糖阴性，而她记录的尿糖阴性与血糖并不相符；即使对已确诊的中枢性尿崩症，英国内分泌学会（2018）也是先用0.9%氯化钠恢复容量，并提醒大量补液时再加去氨加压素可能使高钠纠正过快。
feedback.en: Not now. With a glucose of 33.7 mmol/L the urine cannot yet be read as a pure water loss — the Endocrine Society 2016 criteria for central diabetes insipidus include a urine dipstick negative for glucose, and her recorded negative urine glucose does not fit her blood glucose — and even in known cranial diabetes insipidus the Society for Endocrinology (2018) restores volume with 0.9% sodium chloride first, warning that desmopressin with large fluid loads can correct hypernatraemia too fast.

prompt.zh-CN: 约十天后，她的血糖已控制，但血钠又升到162 mmol/L，每天尿量8.4升。她告诉你，十八年来她每天喝5–8升水。下一步怎么做？
prompt.en: About ten days later her glucose is controlled, but her sodium has risen again to 162 mmol/L and she passes 8.4 L of urine a day. She tells you she has drunk 5–8 L a day for eighteen years. What do you do next?

need.zh-CN: 先看第1天治疗记录和约十天后的病房记录，并问她喝水的情况。
need.en: Read the day-one record and the ward review, and ask her about her drinking.

text.zh-CN: 尿液浓缩障碍：有控制地补水，送检配对的血、尿渗透压，在密切监测血钠下给去氨加压素——不做禁水
text.en: A failure to concentrate urine: controlled water replacement, paired plasma and urine osmolality, and desmopressin with close sodium checks — no water deprivation

feedback.zh-CN: 正确。血糖已控制，就不再有渗透性利尿；习惯性多饮会稀释血浆，而不会让血钠升到162 mmol/L——是她的肾脏没有把尿浓缩。她现在的浓缩程度已经超过禁水试验想要达到的程度——美国内分泌学会2016年方案在血浆渗透压超过295 mOsm/L而尿仍稀释时就停止禁水、给去氨加压素——所以安全的下一步是配对测血、尿渗透压并给去氨加压素，同时补水，使血钠24小时下降不超过10 mmol/L（英国内分泌学会2018）。
feedback.en: Right. With her glucose controlled there is no osmotic diuresis left, and habit drinking dilutes the plasma rather than raising the sodium to 162 mmol/L: her kidneys are not concentrating the urine. She is already more concentrated than a deprivation test sets out to make her — the Endocrine Society 2016 protocol stops thirsting once plasma osmolality passes 295 mOsm/L with dilute urine and gives desmopressin — so the safe next step is paired osmolalities and desmopressin, with water replaced so the sodium falls by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

text.zh-CN: 安排明早做正规禁水试验，以区分尿崩症和习惯性多饮，从午夜起禁食禁饮，保证试验能按时开始
text.en: Book a formal water deprivation test for tomorrow morning to tell diabetes insipidus from habit drinking, keeping her nil by mouth from midnight so that it can start on time

feedback.zh-CN: 危险。血钠162 mmol/L，只按血钠计算（2×162=324），血浆渗透压就已高于美国内分泌学会2016年方案停止禁水的295 mOsm/L——再禁水一夜只会让血钠更高，走向抽搐和循环衰竭，而不会带来任何新信息。
feedback.en: Dangerous. On a sodium of 162 mmol/L alone (2 × 162 = 324) her plasma osmolality is already past the 295 mOsm/L at which the Endocrine Society 2016 protocol stops thirsting — so a night without water can only push her sodium higher, towards seizures and collapse, and adds no information.

text.zh-CN: 十八年来每天喝5–8升，是她一直保持的习惯：每天限水1.5升，停掉所有静脉补液，到周末再复查血钠
text.en: Eighteen years of 5–8 L a day is a habit she has kept up: restrict her to 1.5 L a day, stop all IV fluids and recheck her sodium at the end of the week

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。原发性（习惯性）多饮会使血钠降低；她每天排尿8.4升、血钠却升到162 mmol/L，说明她丢的水比喝进去的多。限水只会让血钠更高——英国内分泌学会（2018）把中枢性尿崩症患者的高钠血症当作需要在高依赖病房处理的急症。
feedback.en: No. Primary (habit) polydipsia lowers the sodium; a sodium that climbs to 162 mmol/L while she passes 8.4 L a day means she is losing more water than she takes in. Restricting her would raise it further — the Society for Endocrinology (2018) manages hypernatraemia in cranial diabetes insipidus as a medical emergency in a high-dependency setting.

text.zh-CN: 仍然是糖尿病在驱动多尿：加强降糖治疗，她每排出一升尿，就补一升0.9%氯化钠
text.en: The diabetes is still driving the urine: step up her glucose-lowering treatment and replace each litre of urine she passes with a litre of 0.9% saline

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。她的血糖已控制，糖尿已解释不了每天8.4升的尿量；用0.9%氯化钠（含钠154 mmol/L，英国内分泌学会2018）一升对一升地补失水，等于给血钠已经162 mmol/L的人再加盐。
feedback.en: No. Her glucose is controlled, so glycosuria no longer explains 8.4 L a day; and replacing a water loss litre for litre with 0.9% saline — 154 mmol/L of sodium (Society for Endocrinology 2018) — adds salt to a woman whose sodium is already 162 mmol/L.

prompt.zh-CN: 记录的试验中，她的尿比重由1.005升至1.020，尿量减少；MRI示空蝶鞍。这些说明什么？长期用去氨加压素之前还要做什么？
prompt.en: On the recorded test her urine specific gravity rose from 1.005 to 1.020 with less urine, and the MRI shows an empty sella. What do these mean, and what must come before long-term desmopressin?

need.zh-CN: 先看试验记录和MRI报告（回答决策3后可以调阅）。
need.en: Read the test record and the MRI report (available once decision 3 is answered).

text.zh-CN: 肾脏能浓缩尿液，符合AVP缺乏（中枢性尿崩症）；空蝶鞍相关但不能证明病因——查垂体前叶功能，先查晨8–9时皮质醇
text.en: Her kidneys can concentrate, fitting AVP deficiency (central diabetes insipidus); the empty sella goes with it but proves no cause — test the anterior pituitary, an 8–9 am cortisol first

feedback.zh-CN: 正确。尿比重升到1.020且尿量减少，说明肾脏有反应——不是AVP抵抗；血糖控制后血钠仍达162 mmol/L，也不符合习惯性多饮。报告的诊断是尿崩症伴空蝶鞍，现在称为AVP缺乏（尿崩症更名工作组，2022）。记录没有说明尿比重是在禁水时还是注射垂体后叶素后才升高；空蝶鞍描述的是结构而不是功能：要检查垂体前叶——先查晨8–9时皮质醇，再查游离T4和TSH（美国内分泌学会2016）——因为漏诊皮质醇缺乏很危险，而糖皮质激素会改变她排水的能力（英国内分泌学会2018）。
feedback.en: Right. A rise to 1.020 with less urine shows kidneys that can respond — not AVP resistance — and a sodium of 162 mmol/L once her glucose was controlled does not fit habit drinking; the report diagnosed diabetes insipidus with an empty sella, now called AVP deficiency (Working Group for Renaming Diabetes Insipidus, 2022). The record does not say whether the rise came with thirsting or only after the extract, and an empty sella describes structure, not function: test the anterior pituitary — an 8–9 am cortisol first, then free T4 with TSH (Endocrine Society 2016) — because a missed cortisol deficiency is dangerous and glucocorticoids change how she excretes water (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

text.zh-CN: 空蝶鞍证明全垂体功能减退：今天就同时开始氢化可的松、左甲状腺素和去氨加压素，不必等化验室把任何一项激素结果报回来
text.en: The empty sella proves panhypopituitarism: start hydrocortisone, levothyroxine and desmopressin together today, without waiting for any of the hormone results to come back from the laboratory

feedback.zh-CN: 不对——影像不等于功能。先检查再治疗：美国内分泌学会2016年指南以晨8–9时皮质醇作为首选检查，并查游离T4和TSH；开始左甲状腺素之前要先评估肾上腺功能（无法评估时先给糖皮质激素），因为甲状腺素可能使未被识别的皮质醇缺乏发展为危象。
feedback.en: No — imaging is not function. Test before treating: the Endocrine Society 2016 guideline uses an 8–9 am cortisol as the first test, with free T4 and TSH, and asks for adrenal insufficiency to be assessed (or glucocorticoid given when it cannot be) before levothyroxine is started, since thyroxine can tip unrecognised cortisol deficiency into a crisis.

text.zh-CN: 她的肾脏对加压素反应差，这是肾性尿崩症：开始噻嗪类利尿剂、低盐饮食，整个治疗过程中都不用去氨加压素
text.en: Her kidneys respond poorly to vasopressin, so this is nephrogenic diabetes insipidus: start a thiazide with a low-salt diet, and keep desmopressin out of her treatment

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。AVP抵抗时，即使给了加压素，尿仍然稀释——美国内分泌学会2016年试验方案中低于300 mOsm/kg——而她的尿比重升到1.020、尿量减少。噻嗪类和限盐用于AVP抵抗，而这里没有任何证据提示AVP抵抗。
feedback.en: No. In AVP resistance the urine stays dilute even after vasopressin — below 300 mOsm/kg in the Endocrine Society 2016 test protocol — whereas hers concentrated to a specific gravity of 1.020 with less urine. Thiazides and salt restriction are for AVP resistance, which nothing here shows.

text.zh-CN: 空蝶鞍是偶然发现，试验已经下了结论：开始去氨加压素后让她出院，几周后门诊复诊时再查血钠
text.en: The empty sella is incidental and the test has settled the question: start desmopressin and send her home, with a sodium check at a clinic visit in a few weeks

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。美国内分泌学会2016年指南把空蝶鞍列为垂体功能减退的病因之一，所以出院前要检查她的垂体前叶功能；而且去氨加压素随时可能造成水潴留——口渴感正常、用去氨加压素的尿崩症患者约四分之一有轻度低钠血症（美国内分泌学会2016）：同一指南要求告诉每位用药患者用药过量的风险，并至少每周安排一段多尿期；血钠要尽早复查，而不是几周后。
feedback.en: No. An empty sella is among the causes of hypopituitarism the Endocrine Society 2016 guideline lists, so her anterior pituitary is tested before she goes; and desmopressin can retain water at any time — about a quarter of patients with diabetes insipidus and intact thirst who take it have mild hyponatraemia (Endocrine Society 2016): the same guideline asks clinicians to teach every patient on desmopressin about overdosing and to build in a phase of polyuria at least weekly, and the sodium is checked early, not weeks later.

prompt.zh-CN: 用去氨加压素后，她每天尿量1.4–2.4升，但觉得头晕，血钠122 mmol/L。你怎么处理？
prompt.en: On desmopressin her urine output is 1.4–2.4 L a day, but she feels dizzy and her sodium is 122 mmol/L. What do you do?

need.zh-CN: 先看后续记录（尿量与血钠），并问问她现在感觉怎么样。
need.en: Read the later record (urine output and sodium) and ask her how she feels.

text.zh-CN: 暂停或减少去氨加压素，饮水以口渴为度，每6小时查血钠，24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L，之后减量重新开始
text.en: Hold or reduce the desmopressin, let her drink only to thirst, check her sodium every 6 hours for a rise of no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours, then restart lower

feedback.zh-CN: 正确。这提示去氨加压素造成的水潴留：先停用或减少诱发药物（欧洲低钠血症指南2014，7.4.1.1）。122 mmol/L属于重度低钠血症；发生时间没有记录，指南按慢性处理，所以第一个24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L，此后每24小时不超过8 mmol/L，每6小时查一次血钠（7.4.1.4–7.4.1.5）——药效一过，快速排水可能使血钠升得过快。之后以更低剂量重新开始，并告诉她用药过量的风险，至少每周安排一段多尿期（美国内分泌学会2016）。
feedback.en: Right. This points to water held by desmopressin: stop or reduce what provokes it (European hyponatraemia guideline 2014, 7.4.1.1). At 122 mmol/L the hyponatraemia is profound; with its duration undocumented the guideline treats it as chronic, so keep the rise to no more than 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L in each 24 hours after, checking sodium every 6 hours (7.4.1.4–7.4.1.5) — once the drug wears off a brisk water diuresis can overshoot. Then restart lower, with teaching about overdosing and a phase of polyuria at least weekly (Endocrine Society 2016).

text.zh-CN: 20分钟内输注3%氯化钠150 mL，反复给直到血钠升高5 mmol/L为止，去氨加压素剂量保持不变，让尿量继续受控
text.en: Give 150 mL of 3% saline over 20 minutes and repeat it until her sodium has risen by 5 mmol/L, keeping the desmopressin dose the same so the urine stays controlled

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。每次150 mL、反复给到血钠升高5 mmol/L，是欧洲指南（2014）用于严重症状（呕吐、深度嗜睡、抽搐、昏迷、心肺窘迫）的治疗；即使是中重度症状（恶心、意识模糊、头痛）也只给一次。头晕不在这两类之列，而且下降时间没有记录，指南按慢性处理。去氨加压素剂量不变，病因就还在。
feedback.en: No. Repeated 150 mL boluses until the sodium has risen by 5 mmol/L are the European guideline's (2014) treatment for severe symptoms — vomiting, deep somnolence, seizures, coma, cardiorespiratory distress — and even moderately severe ones (nausea, confusion, headache) get a single bolus; dizziness is in neither list, and with the timing of the fall undocumented the guideline treats it as chronic. Keeping desmopressin at the same dose leaves its cause in place.

text.zh-CN: 去氨加压素剂量不变，毕竟它终于控制住了尿量，再加用盐片并让她多喝水，使血钠回升
text.en: Keep the same desmopressin dose, since it has finally brought the urine under control, and add salt tablets with plenty of fluids so that her sodium comes back up

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。造成水潴留的药物剂量不变，再多喝水只会加重低钠血症；欧洲指南（2014）首先要停用诱发低钠的药物，而在随意饮水的情况下加盐，并不能去掉多余的水。
feedback.en: No. The drug that is holding water stays at the same dose and more fluid feeds the hyponatraemia; the European guideline (2014) first stops the medicines that provoke it, and extra salt while she drinks freely leaves the water excess in place.

text.zh-CN: 彻底停用去氨加压素，让她想喝多少就喝多少；药效一过血钠会自行恢复，不用再复查
text.en: Stop the desmopressin for good and let her drink as much as she likes; once the drug wears off her sodium will correct itself, so it need not be checked again

feedback.zh-CN: 不对。停药后会重新出现大量排水，122 mmol/L的血钠可能在24小时内升高超过10 mmol/L——超出欧洲指南（2014）的限度，有渗透性脱髓鞘的风险——所以要每6小时查一次血钠；而且她的AVP缺乏仍需治疗：没有去氨加压素时，她的血钠曾升到162 mmol/L。
feedback.en: No. Stopping it lets a water diuresis return, and a sodium of 122 mmol/L can then rise by more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours — beyond the European guideline's (2014) limit, with osmotic demyelination as the risk — so sodium needs checking every 6 hours; and her AVP deficiency still needs treating: without desmopressin her sodium reached 162 mmol/L.

text.zh-CN: 向陪同者问清：她怎样、何时被发现，她的糖尿病和血糖监测，二甲双胍，口干和喝水，以及有没有头部受伤或吃药过量可以解释她的意识不清
text.en: From her companion: how and when she was found, her diabetes and its monitoring, her metformin, her dry mouth and drinking, and whether a head injury or too many tablets could explain her unconsciousness

text.zh-CN: 到院时评估了她的意识、脉搏和血压
text.en: Assessed her consciousness, pulse and blood pressure on arrival

text.zh-CN: 在急诊除基本结果外，还开了渗透压、血酮，以及针对低钾的心电图
text.en: In the emergency department, beyond the basic results: an osmolality, blood ketones and an ECG for the low potassium

text.zh-CN: 首次作答即把首批结果解读为高渗状态加上血糖解释不了的失水（决策1）
text.en: Read the first results at the first attempt as a hyperosmolar state with a water loss the glucose does not explain (decision 1)

text.zh-CN: 离开急诊之前：0.9%氯化钠和补钾已经开始，并已安排每小时监测血糖、血钠和渗透压
text.en: Before she left the emergency department: 0.9% sodium chloride and potassium running, with hourly monitoring of glucose, sodium and osmolality

text.zh-CN: 首次作答即选择安全的第一天方案（决策2）
text.en: Chose a safe plan for the first day at the first attempt (decision 2)

text.zh-CN: 最初几小时、血钾3.2 mmol/L时没有用胰岛素，没有快速输注低渗液体，也没有做禁水试验
text.en: No insulin in the first hours with a potassium of 3.2 mmol/L, no fast hypotonic infusion, and no water deprivation test

text.zh-CN: 安排上级医生评估和高依赖病床，开始预防血栓，并上了心电监护
text.en: Arranged senior review and a high-dependency bed, started thromboprophylaxis and put her on a cardiac monitor

text.zh-CN: 首次作答即判断持续的多尿和高钠意味着什么，以及怎样安全地证实（决策3）
text.en: Worked out at the first attempt what the persisting urine and sodium mean, and how to confirm it safely (decision 3)

text.zh-CN: 在病房：有控制地补水，同时送检血、尿渗透压，并请内分泌团队参与
text.en: On the ward: controlled water replacement, plasma and urine osmolality sent together, and the endocrine team involved

text.zh-CN: 首次作答即正确解读试验和影像（决策4），并开了晨起皮质醇
text.en: Interpreted the test and the scan correctly at the first attempt (decision 4) and ordered a morning cortisol

text.zh-CN: 首次作答即选择怎样纠正用去氨加压素后的低钠（决策5）
text.en: Chose how to correct the low sodium on desmopressin at the first attempt (decision 5)

text.zh-CN: 血钠122 mmol/L、正在用去氨加压素：在查看结局之前就暂停或减少了剂量
text.en: On desmopressin with a sodium of 122 mmol/L: held or reduced the dose before the outcome was read

text.zh-CN: 没有给3%氯化钠；没有在禁忌的时候给去氨加压素、补水或限水
text.en: No 3% saline, and no desmopressin, water replacement or fluid restriction at a time when it was contraindicated

text.zh-CN: 向陪同者和清醒后的她通俗、坦诚地说明病情和不确定性，并确认对方听懂了
text.en: Explained her condition and its uncertainties honestly and in plain words to her companion and, once awake, to her, and checked they understood

judgeGuidance.zh-CN: 按Calgary–Cambridge框架评价两段谈话。与陪同者（急诊）：介绍自己，先问对方知道什么、最担心什么（“她还能醒过来吗？”）；用通俗的话说明她的血糖和血钠都高得危险、为什么意识不清、为什么要慢慢纠正、接下来会做什么，不作虚假保证；问清她平时喝水和吃药的情况。与患者（病房和用药后）：说明她有两种不同的病——一种是糖尿病，另一种是保水激素加压素不足（AVP缺乏，以前叫尿崩症）——以及名字为什么容易混淆；去氨加压素为什么既不能停也不能多用；口渴才喝水；每周让药效过去一次；定期查血钠；随身带病情卡。消息较重时用SPIKES步骤；请对方复述要点以确认理解。本病例没有记录医生对她或陪同者说了什么。
judgeGuidance.en: Judge two conversations against the Calgary–Cambridge guide. With her companion in the emergency department: introduce yourself, ask first what they know and fear ('Will she wake up?'), explain in plain words that her sugar and salt are dangerously high, why she is unconscious, why they must be brought down slowly and what happens next, without false reassurance, and ask what they know about her drinking and medicines. With her, once awake and on desmopressin: explain that she has two different conditions — her diabetes, and a shortage of the water-holding hormone vasopressin (AVP deficiency, once called diabetes insipidus) — and why the names are easily confused; why desmopressin must be neither stopped nor overdosed; drinking to thirst; letting a dose wear off once a week; sodium checks; carrying an alert card. Use SPIKES where the news is heavy, and check understanding by teach-back. This case does not record what she or her companion were told.

name.zh-CN: 乔医生（内分泌科主治医师，化名）

knowledge.zh-CN: 苏格拉底式带教，只围绕学员已经拿到的资料提问，例如：“血钠172时尿比重1.005说明什么？”“pH 7.4配上碳酸氢根36.5，二氧化碳分压大概要多高？这对她的呼吸意味着什么？（本病例没有记录）”“血钾3.2时为什么不马上用胰岛素？”“她的血钠最多能降多快？为什么看速度而不是看数值？”“十天以后，习惯性多饮能让血钠到162吗？”“为什么现在不做禁水试验？”“空蝶鞍能说明什么，不能说明什么？”“为什么长期用去氨加压素之前、用甲状腺素之前要先查皮质醇？”“用去氨加压素后血钠为什么会降，又该以多快的速度回升？”可以讲解JBDS-IP 2022（HHS）、2024年ADA/EASD/JBDS-IP/AACE/DTS共识、英国内分泌学会2018住院中枢性尿崩症指导、美国内分泌学会2016垂体功能减退指南、欧洲2014低钠血症指南，以及2022年改称AVP缺乏的声明。病例结束后按PEARLS框架复盘。报告中的处理是历史记录，学员读到时再与现行指南对照。不提前说出诊断、任何决策的正确选项或结局；她的气道、格拉斯哥昏迷评分、呼吸频率、血氧、体温、体重、尿素、所输液体的种类、是否用过胰岛素或补钾、去氨加压素的剂型和剂量、垂体前叶检查结果和长期结局都没有记录，不要替它补上。
knowledge.en: A Socratic teacher who asks only about what the learner already has, for example: 'What does a urine specific gravity of 1.005 mean beside a sodium of 172?', 'What PCO₂ would make a pH of 7.4 fit a bicarbonate of 36.5, and what would that say about her breathing? It is not recorded.', 'Why not insulin straight away with a potassium of 3.2?', 'How fast may her sodium fall, and why the rate rather than the number?', 'Ten days on, can habit drinking give a sodium of 162?', 'Why not a water deprivation test now?', 'What does an empty sella tell you, and what can it not?', 'Why cortisol before long-term desmopressin, and before thyroxine?', 'Why did her sodium fall on desmopressin, and how fast may it come back up?'. May explain JBDS-IP 2022 (HHS), the 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS-IP/AACE/DTS consensus, the Society for Endocrinology 2018 inpatient cranial diabetes insipidus guidance, the Endocrine Society 2016 hypopituitarism guideline, the European hyponatraemia guideline of 2014 and the 2022 renaming to AVP deficiency. Debriefs with PEARLS once the case is over. The report's management is a historical record, compared with current guidance when the learner reaches it. Never states the diagnosis, a decision's correct option or the outcome early; her airway, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, saturation, temperature, weight, urea, the type of fluid and any insulin or potassium she received, the desmopressin preparation and doses, any anterior pituitary results and the long-term outcome are not recorded — do not supply them.

knowledge.zh-CN: 急诊护士，后来也在病房照护她。交班（ISBAR）：50岁女性，3小时前被发现躺在床上意识不清、双上肢抽搐；一年前查出糖尿病，二甲双胍服用不规律；到院时意识不清，脉搏104次/分，血压121/74 mmHg；陪她来的人在床旁。设备：抢救室有监护仪、氧气和吸引，血糖仪、血酮仪和心电图机就在手边，床旁有输液泵；化验室、CT和MRI可以用；有高依赖病床。可以按医嘱摆体位、保护气道、建立静脉通路、连接监护、测指尖血糖、用输液泵补液补钾、记录每小时数值和出入量、给药。每条医嘱都复述确认；只报告已经发生的情况和已经出来的结果，不解读、不诊断；问到没有记录的内容（格拉斯哥昏迷评分、呼吸频率、血氧、体温、体重、输过什么液体）就如实说没有记录。
knowledge.en: Emergency nurse who later also cares for her on the ward. Handover (ISBAR): a 50-year-old woman found unconscious in bed three hours ago with convulsions of both arms; diabetes found a year ago, metformin taken irregularly; on arrival unconscious, pulse 104/min, blood pressure 121/74 mmHg; the person who came with her is at the bedside. Kit: the bay has a monitor, oxygen and suction; the glucometer, ketone meter and ECG machine are at hand and infusion pumps are at the bed; the laboratory, CT and MRI are available, and there are high-dependency beds. Can, on instruction, position her and protect her airway, put in cannulas, attach the monitor, check a capillary glucose, run fluids and potassium by pump, keep the hourly chart and fluid balance, and give medicines. Reads back every order, reports only what has happened and results that are back, never interprets or diagnoses, and says plainly when something is not recorded (her Glasgow Coma Scale score, breathing rate, saturation, temperature, weight, what fluid she had).

knowledge.zh-CN: 放射科医生，只解读学员已经看过的影像。可以说明：意识不清的患者头颅CT未见异常，并不能排除所有结构性、缺血性或感染性病因，要结合临床；“空蝶鞍”这一术语指蝶鞍看上去被脑脊液充填、垂体受压变扁或难以看清；她的报告只有这一术语，这是结构上的描述，本身不说明激素功能；报告没有描述垂体柄、垂体后叶高信号或所用序列。不说出诊断结论；没有记录的内容不补充。
knowledge.en: Radiologist who interprets only images the learner has already read. Can explain: an unremarkable head CT in an unconscious patient does not exclude every structural, ischaemic or infective cause and must be read with the clinical picture; 'empty sella' is the term for a sella that appears filled with cerebrospinal fluid, the gland flattened or hard to see; her report gives the term only, and it is a structural description that by itself says nothing about hormone function; the report describes neither the pituitary stalk nor the posterior pituitary bright spot, nor the sequences used. Does not state the diagnosis; adds nothing that is not recorded.

title.zh-CN: 复盘：高渗高血糖状态合并AVP缺乏（中枢性尿崩症）与空蝶鞍
title.en: Debrief: hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state with AVP deficiency (central diabetes insipidus) and an empty sella

conclusion.zh-CN: 50岁女性，一年前查出糖尿病，平时没有规律监测血糖，二甲双胍服用不规律，被发现躺在床上意识不清、双上肢抽搐。到院时脉搏104次/分，血压121/74 mmHg；血糖33.7 mmol/L，钠172、钾3.2 mmol/L，肌酐122.9 μmol/L，pH 7.4，碳酸氢根36.5 mmol/L，尿酮阴性，头颅CT未见异常——为高渗高血糖状态。但有两点单纯的高血糖危象解释不了：尿比重1.005；记录的尿糖阴性与血糖不相符，有待核实。首日补液约9 L（尿量4.7 L），次日血钠139 mmol/L，下降幅度远超今天24小时不超过10 mmol/L的限度。经治疗后意识恢复。约十天后血糖已控制，血钠却又升至162 mmol/L，尿量8.4 L/日；追问得知她多饮十八年，每日5–8 L。记录为既往完成的禁水-垂体后叶素试验（何时进行没有记录）中，尿比重由1.005升至1.020、尿量减少，MRI示空蝶鞍；报告诊断为尿崩症，现称AVP缺乏。用去氨加压素后尿量降至每日1.4–2.4 L，但出现头晕、血钠122 mmol/L；减量后血钠135 mmol/L，血糖5.5–7.4 mmol/L。完整的垂体功能评估和更长期的结局没有记录。
conclusion.en: A 50-year-old woman whose diabetes had been found a year earlier — without regular glucose monitoring, and with metformin taken irregularly — was found unconscious in bed with convulsions of both arms. On arrival her pulse was 104/min and blood pressure 121/74 mmHg; glucose 33.7 mmol/L, sodium 172 and potassium 3.2 mmol/L, creatinine 122.9 μmol/L, pH 7.4, bicarbonate 36.5 mmol/L, urine ketones negative and a head CT unremarkable: a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state. Two features did not fit a hyperglycaemic crisis alone: urine of specific gravity 1.005, and a recorded negative urine glucose that does not fit her blood glucose and needs checking. With about 9 L of fluid on day one (urine output 4.7 L) her sodium was 139 mmol/L the next day — a fall well beyond today's limit of 10 mmol/L in 24 hours. She regained consciousness after treatment. About ten days later, with her glucose controlled, her sodium had risen again to 162 mmol/L and she passed 8.4 L of urine a day; further questioning disclosed eighteen years of drinking 5–8 L a day. On a water deprivation and posterior-pituitary extract test recorded as previously completed (when it was done is not recorded), her urine specific gravity rose from 1.005 to 1.020 with less urine, and MRI showed an empty sella; the report diagnosed diabetes insipidus, now called AVP deficiency. Desmopressin brought her urine down to 1.4–2.4 L a day but was followed by dizziness and a sodium of 122 mmol/L; after the dose was reduced her sodium was 135 mmol/L and her glucose 5.5–7.4 mmol/L. A complete assessment of her pituitary function and her longer-term outcome are not recorded.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 意识不清、血糖33.7 mmol/L、无酮症、pH 7.4、有效渗透压2×172+33.7=377.7 mOsm/kg：这是高渗高血糖状态，不是酮症酸中毒。
keyReasoning.en: Unconsciousness with a glucose of 33.7 mmol/L, no ketosis, a pH of 7.4 and an effective osmolality of 2 × 172 + 33.7 = 377.7 mOsm/kg is a hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state, not ketoacidosis.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 高渗的患者本该排出浓缩尿；血钠172 mmol/L时尿比重只有1.005，说明排出的水几乎不带溶质——提示除了血糖还有别的原因。
keyReasoning.en: A hyperosmolar patient should pass concentrated urine; a specific gravity of 1.005 beside a sodium of 172 mmol/L means water is leaving with little solute — a sign that something besides the glucose is at work.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 第一天的安全目标是变化的速度：次日血钠139 mmol/L，正是今天的限速要防止的情况。
keyReasoning.en: On the first day the safety target is the rate of change: a next-day sodium of 139 mmol/L is exactly what today's limits are written to prevent.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 十天后血糖已控制，每天尿量8.4升、血钠162 mmol/L，只剩下尿液浓缩障碍这一解释；习惯性多饮会使血钠降低，而已经这样高渗的患者不需要禁水试验。
keyReasoning.en: Ten days on, with the glucose controlled, 8.4 L of urine a day and a sodium of 162 mmol/L leave a concentrating defect; habit drinking would have lowered the sodium, and a patient this hyperosmolar needs no deprivation test.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 试验中尿液能浓缩，不支持AVP抵抗；空蝶鞍只是结构上的线索，所以要检查垂体前叶，先查皮质醇。
keyReasoning.en: Urine that concentrates on the test points away from AVP resistance; the empty sella is a structural clue, so the anterior pituitary has to be tested, cortisol first.

keyReasoning.zh-CN: 用去氨加压素后血钠122 mmol/L伴头晕，提示药物造成的水潴留：暂停或减量，让血钠慢慢回升。
keyReasoning.en: On desmopressin, a sodium of 122 mmol/L with dizziness points to water retained by the drug: hold or reduce it and let the sodium rise slowly.

teachingPoints.zh-CN: 高渗高血糖状态（JBDS-IP 2022）：血糖通常≥30 mmol/L，渗透压≥320 mOsm/kg［（2×钠）+血糖+尿素］，无明显酮血症或酸中毒。用0.9%氯化钠恢复循环，各项指标都要慢慢降：渗透压每小时下降3–8 mOsm/kg，血糖每小时不超过5 mmol/L（共识为5–6.7），血钠24小时不超过10 mmol/L（JBDS-IP 2022；2024年ADA/EASD/JBDS-IP/AACE/DTS共识）。报告中血钠从172降到次日139 mmol/L，是今天的限速要防止的历史做法。
teachingPoints.en: Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (JBDS-IP 2022): glucose usually ≥30 mmol/L, osmolality ≥320 mOsm/kg [(2 × Na) + glucose + urea], no significant ketonaemia or acidosis. Restore the circulation with 0.9% sodium chloride and bring everything down slowly — osmolality by 3–8 mOsm/kg an hour, glucose by no more than 5 mmol/L an hour (5–6.7 in the consensus), sodium by no more than 10 mmol/L in 24 hours (JBDS-IP 2022; 2024 ADA/EASD/JBDS-IP/AACE/DTS consensus). The report's fall from 172 to 139 mmol/L by the next day is historical practice that today's limits are meant to prevent.

teachingPoints.zh-CN: 先补钾，再用胰岛素：胰岛素会把钾带进细胞。血钾低于3.5 mmol/L时，JBDS-IP 2022要求上级医生评估、补钾量超过常规方案；HHS只有在单纯补液后血糖不再下降时（有明显酮血症除外）才以0.05单位/kg/h开始胰岛素；对酮症酸中毒，2024年共识要求血钾超过3.5 mmol/L再用胰岛素。
teachingPoints.en: Potassium before insulin: insulin moves potassium into cells. Below 3.5 mmol/L, JBDS-IP 2022 asks for senior review and more potassium than its standard regimen, and starts insulin in HHS only once the glucose stops falling on IV fluids alone (unless there is significant ketonaemia), at 0.05 U/kg/h; for ketoacidosis, the 2024 consensus delays insulin until potassium is above 3.5 mmol/L.

teachingPoints.zh-CN: 高渗患者排出稀释尿是警讯：有多尿时要同时测血、尿渗透压——美国内分泌学会2016指出，血浆渗透压高于295 mOsm/L时，尿渗透压应达到约600 mOsm/L（尿/血比值≥2），且尿试纸糖阴性。已经高钠的患者早已越过其禁水方案停止禁水的界值，她需要的是去氨加压素和配对渗透压，而不是禁水。
teachingPoints.en: A dilute urine in a hyperosmolar patient is a warning: with polyuria, measure plasma and urine osmolality together — when plasma osmolality is above 295 mOsm/L, the urine should reach about 600 mOsm/L (urine-to-plasma ratio ≥2), with a urine dipstick negative for glucose (Endocrine Society 2016). A patient already hypernatraemic is past the point at which its deprivation protocol stops; she needs desmopressin and paired osmolalities, not thirsting.

teachingPoints.zh-CN: 口渴保护中枢性尿崩症患者：口渴感正常、能自由饮水时，他们能维持水平衡；意识下降或喝不到水时，可能出现危及生命的脱水（英国内分泌学会2018）。由此看，十八年来每天喝5–8 L更像是代偿，而不是要戒掉的习惯。中枢性尿崩症伴高钠血症是急症，应在高依赖病房处理；无症状或症状轻时，血钠每小时下降不超过0.5 mmol/L、24小时不超过10 mmol/L（英国内分泌学会2018）。
teachingPoints.en: Thirst protects people with cranial diabetes insipidus: with intact thirst and free access to water they keep their balance, while reduced consciousness or limited access to water can bring life-threatening dehydration (Society for Endocrinology 2018). In that light, eighteen years of drinking 5–8 L a day reads as compensation rather than a habit to stop. Hypernatraemia in cranial diabetes insipidus is a medical emergency for a high-dependency setting, corrected by no more than 0.5 mmol/L an hour and 10 mmol/L in 24 hours when symptoms are absent or mild (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

teachingPoints.zh-CN: AVP缺乏伴鞍区异常要检查垂体前叶：首选晨8–9时皮质醇，同时查游离T4和TSH，开始左甲状腺素之前先评估肾上腺功能或给糖皮质激素（美国内分泌学会2016）。糖皮质激素帮助肾脏排出自由水，所以补上隐匿的皮质醇缺乏后，多尿可能才显现出来（英国内分泌学会2018）。
teachingPoints.en: AVP deficiency with an abnormal sella calls for anterior pituitary testing: an 8–9 am cortisol first, free T4 with TSH, and adrenal insufficiency assessed or covered before levothyroxine (Endocrine Society 2016). Glucocorticoids enable free water excretion, so treating a hidden cortisol deficiency can unmask the polyuria (Society for Endocrinology 2018).

teachingPoints.zh-CN: 去氨加压素的安全：最低有效剂量，告诉患者用药过量的风险，至少每周出现一段多尿期（美国内分泌学会2016）。血钠下降时——本例降到122 mmol/L，按欧洲指南（2014）属重度——停用或减量，每6小时查血钠，第一个24小时升幅不超过10 mmol/L、此后每24小时不超过8 mmol/L；报告减量后血钠为135 mmol/L。AVP缺乏（2022年更名）不是糖尿病：两者混淆曾导致去氨加压素被停用，甚至有患者死亡。
teachingPoints.en: Desmopressin safety: the lowest effective dose, teaching about overdosing, and a phase of polyuria at least weekly (Endocrine Society 2016). If the sodium falls — here to 122 mmol/L, profound by the European guideline (2014) — stop or reduce the drug, check sodium every 6 hours and keep the rise within 10 mmol/L in the first 24 hours and 8 mmol/L in each 24 hours after; after the report's dose reduction her sodium was 135 mmol/L. AVP deficiency (renamed in 2022) is not diabetes mellitus: confusing the two has led to desmopressin being withheld, with deaths.

boundaries.zh-CN: 这是单例报告，本版本的事实只来自1.0.0版的提取，尚未对照原文全文核对：它不能说明她AVP缺乏的病因、空蝶鞍与之的关系、垂体前叶是否受累，也不能说明血钠纠正过快是否对她造成了损害。报告的处理作为历史事实保留，并对照现行指南讲授；本病例不构成对任何个体患者的建议。
boundaries.en: A single case report, and in this version its facts come only from the version 1.0.0 extraction, not yet checked against the full article: it cannot show what caused her AVP deficiency, how the empty sella relates to it, whether her anterior pituitary was affected, or whether the fast sodium correction harmed her. The report's management is kept as historical fact and taught against current guidance; nothing here is advice for an individual patient.

unknowns.zh-CN: 她到院时的气道、格拉斯哥昏迷评分、呼吸频率、血氧饱和度和体温，以及体重。
unknowns.en: Her airway, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and temperature on arrival, and her weight.

unknowns.zh-CN: 尿素、氯，渗透压“392”的标本、单位和测定方法，二氧化碳分压，以及血气是动脉血还是静脉血。
unknowns.en: Urea, chloride, the specimen, unit and method of the osmolality of 392, the PCO₂, and whether the blood gas was arterial or venous.

unknowns.zh-CN: 血糖33.7 mmol/L时为什么尿糖记录为阴性。
unknowns.en: Why the urine glucose was recorded as negative with a blood glucose of 33.7 mmol/L.

unknowns.zh-CN: 第1天输的液体（种类、途径、速度）、是否用过胰岛素和补钾，以及每小时的血钠和血糖。
unknowns.en: The fluids given on day one (type, route, rate), any insulin or potassium, and the hourly sodium and glucose.

unknowns.zh-CN: 这次危象的诱因；是谁发现了她；陪她来的人和她是什么关系。
unknowns.en: What precipitated the crisis; who found her; how the person who came with her is related to her.

unknowns.zh-CN: 禁水-垂体后叶素试验是什么时候做的、禁水多久、垂体后叶素的剂量，以及尿比重是在试验的哪个阶段升高的。
unknowns.en: When the deprivation and extract test was done, how long water was withheld, the extract's dose, and in which part of the test the specific gravity rose.

unknowns.zh-CN: 垂体前叶功能检查（皮质醇、甲状腺、性腺、催乳素、生长激素），以及MRI对垂体柄和垂体后叶的描述。
unknowns.en: Any anterior pituitary tests (cortisol, thyroid, gonadal axis, prolactin, growth hormone), and the MRI's description of the pituitary stalk and posterior pituitary.

unknowns.zh-CN: 她到院时的气道、格拉斯哥昏迷评分、呼吸频率、血氧饱和度和体温，以及体重。
unknowns.en: Her airway, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation and temperature on arrival, and her weight.

unknowns.zh-CN: 尿素、氯，渗透压“392”的标本、单位和测定方法，二氧化碳分压，以及血气是动脉血还是静脉血。
unknowns.en: Urea, chloride, the specimen, unit and method of the osmolality of 392, the PCO₂, and whether the blood gas was arterial or venous.

unknowns.zh-CN: 血糖33.7 mmol/L时为什么尿糖记录为阴性。
unknowns.en: Why the urine glucose was recorded as negative with a blood glucose of 33.7 mmol/L.

unknowns.zh-CN: 第1天输的液体（种类、途径、速度）、是否用过胰岛素和补钾，以及每小时的血钠和血糖。
unknowns.en: The fluids given on day one (type, route, rate), any insulin or potassium, and the hourly sodium and glucose.

unknowns.zh-CN: 这次危象的诱因；是谁发现了她；陪她来的人和她是什么关系。
unknowns.en: What precipitated the crisis; who found her; how the person who came with her is related to her.

unknowns.zh-CN: 禁水-垂体后叶素试验是什么时候做的、禁水多久、垂体后叶素的剂量，以及尿比重是在试验的哪个阶段升高的。
unknowns.en: When the deprivation and extract test was done, how long water was withheld, the extract's dose, and in which part of the test the specific gravity rose.

unknowns.zh-CN: 垂体前叶功能检查（皮质醇、甲状腺、性腺、催乳素、生长激素），以及MRI对垂体柄和垂体后叶的描述。
unknowns.en: Any anterior pituitary tests (cortisol, thyroid, gonadal axis, prolactin, growth hormone), and the MRI's description of the pituitary stalk and posterior pituitary.

unknowns.en: The desmopressin preparation and doses, the time course of the fall to 122 mmol/L and of the recovery to 135 mmol/L, and any longer-term follow-up.
